content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?The Two Pennies's PostThe Two PenniesAugust 22, 2025 · Shared with PublicThe Apache, called Apachú by the Zuni, called themselves Diné — “The People.”Their nations spanned deserts and mountains of the Southwest, divided into bands like Chiricahua, Mescalero, Lipan, Jicarilla, Western Apache, Kiowa Apache, and Navajo. All spoke Athabaskan dialects, tracing back to northern roots.Desert life demanded endurance. The Apache hunted, gathered, and adapted to scarce resources, moving swiftly and silently. Reverence for nature guided them, honoring sacred animals: eagle, bear, coyote, cougar, falcon, and bison.As warriors, they became frontier legends. Masters of ambush, wielding bows, lances, and rifles, they inspired respect and fear among neighbors and Spanish, Mexican, and American forces who sought to conquer their lands.For centuries, the Apache resisted colonial expansion, proving the desert belonged to those strong enough to endure it.#NativeHistory #Apache~ The Two PenniesAll reactions:1.6K81 comments134 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Kathy Rawlings-BuntinNavajos are also the Dine’.
